description: Parquet file format decomposed. Row groups + column chunks + pages. Dictionary encoding + RLE + bit packing + Snappy/Zstd cascade. Statistics + min/max + bloom filters per column chunk. Dremel-style nested schema. Predicate + projection pushdown.

sub_mechanisms.name: file_structure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Parquet file: header (magic 'PAR1') + row groups + footer (schema + metadata + row group offsets). Read footer first, then targeted reads.
sub_mechanisms.why: Footer-based layout: reader knows full schema + chunk locations after small footer read. Enables predicate pushdown (skip row groups via stats) + projection pushdown (read only needed columns).

sub_mechanisms.name: row_group
sub_mechanisms.definition: Horizontal partition of file. Each row group holds N rows (typically 100K-1M). Within a row group: one column chunk per column.
sub_mechanisms.why: Parallelism unit: different row groups can be processed in parallel. Stats per row group enable skipping. Typical size 128 MB-1 GB. Tuned for engine + workload.

sub_mechanisms.name: column_chunk
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-column contiguous storage within a row group. Holds N rows for that column, encoded + compressed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Columnar layout: read one column without reading others. Each chunk has its own encoding + compression. Critical for projection pushdown.

sub_mechanisms.name: page_within_chunk
sub_mechanisms.definition: Smaller unit within column chunk. Default ~1 MB. Each page has its own dictionary (if used) + encoding + compression.
sub_mechanisms.why: Finer granularity for parallel decode + memory streaming. Page-level statistics for predicate filtering. Some readers stream pages without loading whole chunk.

sub_mechanisms.name: dictionary_encoding_parquet
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-chunk dictionary of distinct values. Column values stored as dict indices (typically 1-4 bytes).
sub_mechanisms.why: Low-cardinality columns shrink dramatically. status column with 5 values: 5 × value_size dictionary + N × 1 byte indices vs N × full values. 5-50x compression typical.

sub_mechanisms.name: RLE_in_parquet
sub_mechanisms.definition: Run-Length Encoding: store (value, count) pairs for runs of same value. Used for dictionary indices + sparse columns.
sub_mechanisms.why: After dictionary encoding, sorted or sparse columns have long runs. RLE compresses them. Combined with bit-packing for further savings.

sub_mechanisms.name: bit_packing_parquet
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pack dictionary indices into minimum bits. 8 distinct values = 3 bits per index, not 8.
sub_mechanisms.why: Indices are small integers; standard byte storage wastes bits. Parquet's RLE/bit-pack hybrid encoding switches between modes per run.

sub_mechanisms.name: snappy_zstd_compression_parquet
sub_mechanisms.definition: After encoding, apply general compression: Snappy (fast), Zstd (balanced), Gzip (legacy), LZ4, Brotli.
sub_mechanisms.why: Encoding does structural compression; general compression cleans up. Cascade is what makes Parquet 5-10x smaller than CSV. Choice trades CPU vs size.

sub_mechanisms.name: column_statistics
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-column-chunk: min, max, null count, distinct count (sometimes). Stored in footer.
sub_mechanisms.why: Predicate pushdown: WHERE col > 100 + stats showing max(col) = 50 → skip entire chunk. 100-1000x speedup on selective queries. The single most impactful Parquet feature.

sub_mechanisms.name: bloom_filter_in_parquet
sub_mechanisms.definition: Optional per-column-chunk bloom filter. Added to Parquet spec in 2019.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stats handle ranges (min/max); bloom handles point lookups. WHERE col = 'X' + bloom says 'not present' → skip chunk. Particularly valuable for high-cardinality string columns.

sub_mechanisms.name: Dremel_nested_schema
sub_mechanisms.definition: Repetition + definition levels encode nested + nullable structure. Each value paired with (rep, def) levels.
sub_mechanisms.why: JSON-like nested data in columnar layout. Each leaf field becomes a column; rep/def reconstruct structure. Standard in Parquet (from Google Dremel paper) — handles arbitrary JSON-like nesting.

sub_mechanisms.name: predicate_projection_pushdown
sub_mechanisms.definition: Engines read only needed columns (projection) and skip row groups whose stats don't match predicate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Spark / Trino / DuckDB / Pandas all do this. SELECT a FROM t WHERE b > 100 reads col 'a' only, only from row groups where max(b) > 100. Dramatic perf win.

derivation_rules.name: Parquet_compression_cascade_shrinks_dramatically
if: columnar + dictionary + RLE + bit-pack + Snappy applied
then: typical file is 5-10x smaller than CSV
derivation_rules.why: Each layer compresses the previous output. Columnar enables better general compression (similar values together). Encoding shrinks structural waste. General compression cleans up. Compound effect.

derivation_rules.name: column_stats_enable_predicate_pushdown
if: query has predicate on column with stats
then: row groups outside predicate range are skipped
derivation_rules.why: Read footer (small) → check stats per row group → skip whole row groups. SELECTIVE queries on indexed-like columns 100-1000x faster than full scan. The reason Parquet beats CSV on analytical workloads.

derivation_rules.name: row_group_size_balances_parallelism_and_overhead
derivation_rules.why: Many small row groups: more parallelism but per-group overhead. Few large: less parallelism, more efficient. Common: 128 MB-1 GB row groups. Engine + storage tier determine optimum.

derivation_rules.name: dictionary_encoding_optimal_for_low_cardinality
if: a column has few distinct values
derivation_rules.why: K distinct values: dictionary of K + log_2(K) bits per row. For status column with 10 values: 4 bits per row. 1000 rows × 10 bytes (string) = 10KB → 4KB indices + tiny dict. 60% smaller before general compression.

derivation_rules.name: Dremel_levels_handle_arbitrary_nesting
then: rep/def levels encode structure in columnar layout
derivation_rules.why: JSON-like {a: [{b: [1,2], c: null}]} flattens to columns with per-value rep/def levels. Reader reconstructs structure. Parquet handles real-world JSON-shaped data without storing JSON.
